title: Lesson 0: Summer Camp Intro + Hub Walkthrough

slides.title: Welcome to AI Future Summer Camp
slides.body: Today we will learn the camp rules, how the Summer Camp Hub works, how to join live lessons, how to submit work, and how points are earned.

slides.title: The 3 Big Rules
slides.body: Be Safe. Be Kind. Be a Builder. These rules guide how we use tools, work with teammates, and improve our designs.

slides.title: Rule Check: Be Safe
slides.body: Which choice shows safe camp behavior?
options: Walk, use tools correctly, and ask a coach if unsure
Run across the room with LEGO pieces
Put small parts near your mouth
Use tools before a coach explains them

slides.title: Rule Check: Be Kind
slides.body: What should you do when a teammate has an idea?
options: Listen, take turns, and build on the idea respectfully
Ignore them and grab the pieces
Tell them their idea is bad

slides.title: Rule Check: Be a Builder
slides.body: What should builders do when their first design does not work?
options: Test, change one thing, and try again
Change everything at once without testing

slides.title: When You Need Help
slides.body: If you are confused, stuck, or unsure about a tool, what should you do?
options: Ask a coach or teammate for help
Leave your group without saying anything

slides.title: How the Summer Hub Works
slides.body: Students log in, see the current week, join live lessons, answer questions, submit reflections and photos, check points, and use resources.

slides.title: Hub Check
slides.body: What should you use to get into the Student Hub?

slides.title: Live Lesson Check
slides.body: What happens when your coach starts a live question?
options: You tap an answer on your iPad

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full intro deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%200/lesson0_intro_slides.html

title: Week 1 - Monday: Intro to LEGO Technic

slides.title: Intro to LEGO Technic
slides.body: Today we build: Tallest Tower. Build the tallest freestanding Technic tower that stays stable for 10 seconds.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build the tallest freestanding Technic tower that stays stable for 10 seconds.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Beams are the long structural pieces. Pins are the connectors that hold beams together. Wide bases and diagonal braces help structures stay stable.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: learn how LEGO Technic beams and pins connect, then build the tallest freestanding tower that can stand on its own for 10 seconds.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Same floor, same tower rules, hands off for 10 seconds, measure only after the tower stands on its own.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: If the tower leans, widen the base, tighten weak joints, or add a diagonal brace before testing again.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%201/lesson1_lego_technic_assets_version.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What made your tower stronger? What was the single best change you made?

slides.title: Wide base
slides.body: Why does a wide base help a tall tower stay up?
options: It spreads out the weight so the tower is harder to tip over
It automatically makes the tower taller

slides.title: Rigid
slides.body: What does it mean for a tower to be "rigid"?
options: It does not bend, wiggle, or twist

slides.title: Measuring
slides.body: In the Tallest Tower challenge, how is the height measured?
options: From the table to the highest connected LEGO piece
From your hand to the ceiling

slides.title: Bridge Engineering
slides.body: Today we build: Strongest Bridge. Build a bridge that spans the gap and holds the most load without collapsing.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a bridge that spans the gap and holds the most load without collapsing.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A support carries weight down to the table or floor. A brace helps a structure keep its shape. Triangles resist bending better than squares.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: engineer a Technic bridge across a gap and test how triangles, supports, and bracing help it hold more weight.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same gap, same load pieces, and add weight one piece at a time until the bridge bends or fails.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Find the weak spot, then add a brace or support there before the next trial.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%202/lesson2_bridge_assets_version.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Where did your bridge fail first? How did triangles or supports change the result?

slides.title: Strong shape
slides.body: Which shape makes a bridge more rigid?

slides.title: Tension
slides.body: What does "tension" mean in a bridge?
options: A part is being pulled or stretched
A part is being pushed or squeezed

slides.title: Bridge rule
slides.body: The bridge challenge says you must use at least how many triangles?

slides.title: Balloon Powered Car
slides.body: Today we build: Balloon-Powered Car. Build a balloon-powered car that rolls as far as possible from one release.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a balloon-powered car that rolls as far as possible from one release.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: An axle lets wheels spin. Friction slows motion. Air rushing out of the balloon pushes the car forward.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a car powered only by air from a balloon, then tune the frame, wheels, and balloon direction for the farthest roll.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same start line, same floor, and one balloon release per trial. Measure total distance traveled.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Free sticky wheels, aim the balloon straight backward, reduce extra weight, and test one change at a time.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%203/lesson3_spike_prime_assets_version.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What caused the car to go straight or curve? Which change improved distance the most?

slides.title: Why it moves
slides.body: Why does the balloon car move forward?
options: Air rushes backward, so the car is pushed forward (action and reaction)
The balloon pulls the car along

slides.title: Axles
slides.body: What are axles best for?

slides.title: Slows it down
slides.body: What is most likely to slow your car down?
options: Friction from wheels rubbing on beams

slides.title: Catapult Engineering
slides.body: Today we build: Catapult. Build a catapult that launches a soft target into a target zone safely and repeatedly.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a catapult that launches a soft target into a target zone safely and repeatedly.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A lever swings around a pivot. Stored energy is energy waiting to be released, like a stretched rubber band.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a safe Technic catapult that uses a lever and stored energy to launch a soft target toward a marked zone.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same soft target, same start position, and same target zone. Track both distance and accuracy.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Change the arm length, rubber band stretch, or base stability one at a time.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%204/lesson4_catapult_assets_version.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What made your launch more accurate? What made it go farther?

slides.title: Stored energy
slides.body: Before launch, where is the energy stored?
options: In the stretched rubber band as elastic potential energy

slides.title: Fulcrum
slides.body: What is the fulcrum of a catapult?
options: The pivot point the arm turns around

slides.title: Stable first
slides.body: Why build a wide, strong base for your catapult?
options: So it stays stable and doesn't tip when the arm swings

slides.title: Rubber Band Car
slides.body: Today we build: Rubber Band Car. Build a car powered only by a wound rubber band.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a car powered only by a wound rubber band.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Elastic energy is stored when a rubber band stretches or twists. Traction helps wheels push against the floor instead of slipping.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a rubber-band-powered car and test how stored elastic energy turns into distance and speed.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same start line and floor. Count winds consistently and measure distance after release.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Adjust wheel size, traction, frame weight, or number of winds one change at a time.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%205/lesson5_rubber_band_car.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Did your car need more speed, more grip, or less friction?

slides.title: Energy source
slides.body: How does the rubber band car get its energy to move?
options: Twisting the rubber band stores elastic energy that turns the axle

slides.title: Fair test
slides.body: What is the rule for keeping a test fair?
options: Change only one thing at a time
Use a different floor each time
Let some teams push the car

slides.title: More twists?
slides.body: Do more rubber band twists always make the car go farther?
options: Not always — too many twists can slip or hurt the run
Yes, more twists is always farther

title: Windmill: Your First SPIKE Prime Program

slides.title: Elevator / Lift
slides.body: Today we build: Elevator / Lift. Raise a small load as high and smoothly as possible.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Raise a small load as high and smoothly as possible.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A pulley changes the direction of a pull. A winch winds string around an axle to lift a load.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build an elevator or lift that raises a small cargo load smoothly and safely.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same cargo load and measure from the floor or table to the final raised height.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Add guides, reduce rubbing, strengthen the tower, or improve the crank.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%206/lesson6_elevator_lift.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What kept the lift from tipping, jamming, or dropping the load?

slides.title: Motor block
slides.body: Which block makes the windmill motor actually turn on?

slides.title: Motor speed
slides.body: You change the motor speed from 50% to 100%. What happens to the windmill?

slides.title: Direction
slides.body: How do you make the motor spin the other way (reverse the direction)?

slides.title: Ferris Wheel
slides.body: Today we build: Ferris Wheel. Build a balanced rotating wheel with a strong axle support.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a balanced rotating wheel with a strong axle support.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Rotation is spinning around an axis. Balance means weight is spread so the wheel does not wobble or fall to one side.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a Ferris wheel that rotates smoothly, stays balanced, and carries small passenger cars.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Turn the wheel through a full rotation and watch for wobble, rubbing, or uneven weight.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Center the axle, balance opposite sides, and strengthen the support frame.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%207/lesson7_ferris_wheel.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Where did the wheel wobble? How did balance change the spin?

slides.title: Smooth spin
slides.body: What helps a Ferris wheel spin smoothly?
options: Supporting the axle on both sides

slides.title: Even pods
slides.body: Why space the passenger pods evenly around the wheel?
options: To keep it balanced so one side doesn't pull harder

slides.title: Wobble
slides.body: What is most likely to make the wheel wobble?
options: Uneven weight or a bending axle

slides.title: Marble Run
slides.body: Today we build: Marble Run. Build a marble run with the longest reliable ride time.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a marble run with the longest reliable ride time.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Gravity pulls the marble downward. Slope controls speed. Barriers keep the marble on the track.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: design a marble run that uses gravity, slope, barriers, and supports to create the longest reliable ride.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same marble and start point. Time from release to finish only if the marble completes the run.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Lower steep sections, add walls at failure points, and strengthen sagging supports.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%208/lesson8_marble_run.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Which part of the track controlled speed best? Where did reliability improve?

slides.title: What moves it
slides.body: What makes the marble move down the run?
options: Gravity pulling it down the slope

slides.title: Steeper slope
slides.body: What does a steeper slope do to the marble?

slides.title: Stay on track
slides.body: What keeps the marble on the path at turns?
options: Guardrails or barriers along the turns

slides.title: Boat / Raft
slides.body: Today we build: Boat / Raft. Build a floating platform that carries cargo without sinking or tipping.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a floating platform that carries cargo without sinking or tipping.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Buoyancy is the upward push of water. Balance keeps weight spread so the raft does not tip.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a boat or raft that floats, stays balanced, and carries as much cargo as possible.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same water bin and same cargo pieces. Add cargo one piece at a time until the raft fails.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Spread the load, widen the raft, lower the center of mass, or add flotation support.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%209/lesson9_boat_raft.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What made the raft tip or sink? What design carried the most load?

slides.title: Floating
slides.body: What helps a raft float and get upward support from the water?
options: Buoyancy — the raft pushes water away

slides.title: Heavy parts
slides.body: Where should the heavy parts sit on a raft?

slides.title: Less tipping
slides.body: What makes a raft harder to tip over?

slides.title: Gripper
slides.body: Today we build: Gripper. Build a hand-operated mechanism that can pick up, hold, move, and release an object.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a hand-operated mechanism that can pick up, hold, move, and release an object.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A pivot is a turning point. A linkage connects parts so one motion creates another motion.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a gripper that opens, closes, picks up objects, and releases them with control.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same test objects and count a success only when the gripper lifts and releases under control.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Adjust jaw shape, add friction at the tips, strengthen pivots, or change linkage length.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2010/lesson10_gripper.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What helped the gripper hold without crushing or dropping the object?

slides.title: Jaw motion
slides.body: What lets each gripper jaw open and close?
options: A pivot point it rotates around

slides.title: Holding on
slides.body: What helps the gripper hold an object without dropping it?
options: Friction from grip surfaces like rubber or tires

slides.title: Even close
slides.body: So the jaws close evenly on the object, they should be...
options: Mirrored — left and right built the same

slides.title: Arm with Gripper
slides.body: Today we build: Arm with Gripper. Move an object from one zone to another using a stable arm and gripper.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Move an object from one zone to another using a stable arm and gripper.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Leverage changes how force works across an arm. A longer arm reaches farther but can tip or bend more easily.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: combine an arm and gripper so the mechanism can reach, lift, move, and release a small object.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same object and target zones. Count success when the arm moves the object without dropping it.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Widen the base, shorten weak arm sections, strengthen joints, or improve the gripper tips.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2011/lesson11_arm_with_gripper.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What was the hardest part: reaching, lifting, gripping, or releasing?

slides.title: Longer reach
slides.body: What happens when the arm reaches farther out?
options: It can reach more but is harder to support and may tip

slides.title: Stay stable
slides.body: What keeps the arm from tipping when it reaches out?

slides.title: Payload
slides.body: The object the arm carries at its end is called the...

slides.title: Simple Car
slides.body: Today we build: Simple Car. Build a reliable rolling chassis that travels straight and stays together.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a reliable rolling chassis that travels straight and stays together.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A chassis is the car frame. Wheelbase is the distance between front and rear axles. Parallel axles help the car roll straight.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build a sturdy simple car chassis that rolls straight and can become the base for sensor and steering challenges.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Push from the same start line and watch whether the car rolls straight, curves, wobbles, or drags.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Straighten axles, free rubbing wheels, strengthen the frame, and leave room for a hub or sensor.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2012/lesson12_simple_car.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Why does a robot car need a strong, straight chassis before it gets sensors?

slides.title: Chassis
slides.body: What is the chassis of a car?
options: The frame that holds everything together

slides.title: Roll straight
slides.body: What helps a car roll straight?

slides.title: Square frame
slides.body: What does a square, braced frame prevent?

title: Week 4 - Monday: Car with Distance Sensor

slides.title: Car with Distance Sensor
slides.body: Today we build: Car with Distance Sensor. Program a car to drive forward and stop before touching a wall.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Program a car to drive forward and stop before touching a wall.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A distance sensor measures how far away an object is. A threshold is the number where the program changes behavior.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: add a SPIKE Prime distance sensor to a car and program it to stop before hitting an obstacle.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same wall, same start line, and same speed. Measure where the car stops.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Change the distance threshold, slow the car, aim the sensor, or clear LEGO from the sensor view.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2013/lesson13_distance_sensor_car.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What threshold stopped the car safely without stopping too early?

slides.title: Threshold
slides.body: In "input, threshold, response," what does the threshold do?
options: Checks if the distance is smaller than a chosen number
Measures the color of the floor

slides.title: Mounting
slides.body: How should the distance sensor be mounted?
options: Facing forward with a clear view, not blocked

slides.title: Input
slides.body: The sensor measuring how far away an object is — that part is the...

title: Week 4 - Tuesday: Car with Color Sensor

slides.title: Car with Color Sensor
slides.body: Today we build: Car with Color Sensor. Program a car to respond when its color sensor sees a marker.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Program a car to respond when its color sensor sees a marker.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: A color sensor reads the color beneath it. Detection works best when the sensor is close, centered, and moving slowly enough.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: add a color sensor to a car and program it to react to floor colors or line markers.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same colored tape, sensor height, and speed for each trial before changing one variable.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Lower the sensor, slow the car, center it over the tape, or improve the color contrast.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2014/lesson14_color_sensor_car.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: What made the color easier or harder for the robot to read?

slides.title: Sensor height
slides.body: A color sensor reads best when it is...
options: Close to the floor with a small gap (not dragging)

slides.title: Calibration
slides.body: What can change a color reading?
options: Lighting and the surface or marker color

slides.title: The challenge
slides.body: In the challenge, the rover should...
options: React differently to different color markers

slides.title: Self-Parking Steering Car
slides.body: Today we build: Self-Parking Steering Car. Build a steering car that parks itself inside a target box.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Build a steering car that parks itself inside a target box.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Steering turns the front wheels. Turning radius is the size of the curve the car makes. A sequence is a set of programmed steps in order.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: build steering control and tune a driving sequence so the car parks inside a marked box.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same start pose and parking box. Run the same sequence until changing one distance, angle, or time.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Tune steering angle, drive distance, speed, and straighten timing one change at a time.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2015/lesson15_self_parking_steering_car.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Which step controlled parking accuracy the most?

slides.title: Linkage
slides.body: What does a steering linkage do?
options: Makes both front wheels turn together

slides.title: Turning radius
slides.body: A sharper steering angle gives you a...
options: Tighter turn, but it can be harder to control

slides.title: Recover
slides.body: After making a turn, the front wheels should...

slides.title: Steering Race
slides.body: Today we build: Steering Race. Complete the race course with the best balance of speed and control.

slides.title: Mission Goal
slides.body: Complete the race course with the best balance of speed and control.

slides.title: Key Ideas
slides.body: Control means the car does what you intend. Reliability means it can repeat a run without falling apart or leaving the course.

slides.title: Build Brief
slides.body: Project: tune a steering car for a course where control, reliability, and clean driving matter as much as speed.

slides.title: Fair Testing
slides.body: Use the same course and start line. Track clean completion before comparing speed.

slides.title: Improve Your Design
slides.body: Slow down for turns, tighten loose joints, improve steering return, and practice consistent starts.

slides.title: Teacher Deck
slides.body: Full teacher deck: /camp-hub/lessons/Lesson%2016/lesson16_steering_race.html

slides.title: Reflect and Share
slides.body: Where did control matter more than speed? What are you proudest of from the four weeks?

slides.title: Wins races
slides.body: What makes a winning race design over many runs?
options: Reliability — it survives repeated runs without falling apart

slides.title: Stay low
slides.body: Why keep a race car low to the ground?
options: It is less likely to tip during turns

title: Claw with a Button: Events in SPIKE

slides.title: Events
slides.body: When does the code under "when left button pressed" run?
options: Every time the left button is pressed
Only once when the program starts

slides.title: Open the claw
slides.body: The claw closes with "run for 1 rotation". How do you make it OPEN again?
options: Run the motor for -1 rotations (negative = other way)

slides.title: Two stacks
slides.body: Why does the claw program need TWO event stacks?
options: One event closes the claw, a different event opens it
Two stacks make the motor stronger

slides.title: Prosthetics
slides.body: What is a prosthetic?
options: A human-made body part that helps someone grab, hold, or walk

slides.title: Inputs
slides.body: The button and the color sensor are both...
options: Inputs that tell the Hub when to act

slides.title: Cool fact
slides.body: Which of these prosthetics facts is TRUE?
options: A 3,000-year-old wooden prosthetic toe was found on an Egyptian mummy
Robotic arms cannot be controlled by muscles
